\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{предыдущий} (predydúshchiy)}{предыдущий (predydúshchiy)}]{\ru{предыдущий} (predydúshchiy) — previous}

\label{lesson:RU-C277-predydushchiy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for an interval, then the Russian for a deadline.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{предыдущий}}
\textbf{\ru{предыдущий}} (\emph{predydúshchiy}) — \textquotedblleft{}previous\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Предыдущий} \ru{урок} \ru{был} \ru{очень} \ru{длинным}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Predydúshchiy urók byl óchen dlínnym.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The previous lesson was very long.
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech also \emph{\ru{прошлый}}. The opposite is \emph{\ru{следующий}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{предыдущий}} is usually described as a Church Slavonic participle, built on \emph{\ru{пред}-} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} and \emph{\ru{идти}} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Proto-Slavic \emph{jĭti} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): the one going before.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{predydúshchiy}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for an interval, then the Russian for a deadline, then say \emph{predydúshchiy} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{последующий} (posléduyushchiy)}{последующий (posléduyushchiy)}]{\ru{последующий} (posléduyushchiy) — following, subsequent}

\label{lesson:RU-C277-posleduyushchiy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a deadline, then the Russian for previous.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{последующий}}
\textbf{\ru{последующий}} (\emph{posléduyushchiy}) — \textquotedblleft{}following, subsequent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{В} \ru{последующие} \ru{дни} \ru{было} \ru{тепло}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{V posléduyushchiye dni býlo tepló.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the following days it was warm.
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{\ru{следующий}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{последующий}} is the participle of \emph{\ru{последовать}} \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{\ru{след}} \textquotedblleft{}a track\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): coming in the footsteps.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{очередной} (ocherednóy)}{очередной (ocherednóy)}]{\ru{очередной} (ocherednóy) — next (in a series), yet another}

\label{lesson:RU-C277-ocherednoy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for previous, then the Russian for following.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{очередной}}
\textbf{\ru{очередной}} (\emph{ocherednóy}) — \textquotedblleft{}next (in a series), yet another\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Он} \ru{рассказал} \ru{очередную} \ru{смешную} \ru{историю}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{On rasskazál ocherednúyu smeshnúyu istóriyu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He told yet another funny story.
\end{quote}

The next in a regular series, or \textquotedblleft{}one more\textquotedblright{}, often a little ironic.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{очередной}} is built on \emph{\ru{очередь}} \textquotedblleft{}a queue, a turn\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{\ru{черёд}}, \emph{\ru{череда}} \textquotedblleft{}a row, a turn\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to Proto-Slavic \emph{čerda} \textquotedblleft{}a file, a herd\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no parent for \emph{\ru{очередной}} itself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{ежегодный} (yezhegódnyy)}{ежегодный (yezhegódnyy)}]{\ru{ежегодный} (yezhegódnyy) — annual, yearly}

\label{lesson:RU-C277-yezhegodnyy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for following, then the Russian for next.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{ежегодный}}
\textbf{\ru{ежегодный}} (\emph{yezhegódnyy}) — \textquotedblleft{}annual, yearly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Ежегодный} \ru{концерт} \ru{будет} \ru{в} \ru{мае}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Yezhegódnyy kontsért búdet v máye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The annual concert will be in May.
\end{quote}

Also \emph{\ru{ежедневный}} — daily, \emph{\ru{еженедельный}} — weekly.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{ежегодный}} is built on \emph{\ru{еже}-} \textquotedblleft{}each\textquotedblright{} and \emph{\ru{год}} \textquotedblleft{}year\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited through Old East Slavic \emph{godŭ} from Proto-Slavic \emph{godŭ} \textquotedblleft{}the right time\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{дальнейший} (dalnéyshiy)}{дальнейший (dalnéyshiy)}]{\ru{дальнейший} (dalnéyshiy) — further, subsequent}

\label{lesson:RU-C277-dalneyshiy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for next, then the Russian for annual.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{дальнейший}}
\textbf{\ru{дальнейший}} (\emph{dalnéyshiy}) — \textquotedblleft{}further, subsequent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{О} \ru{дальнейших} \ru{планах} \ru{он} \ru{не} \ru{говорил}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{O dalnéyshikh plánakh on ne govoríl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He did not talk about further plans.
\end{quote}

\emph{\ru{В} \ru{дальнейшем}} — in future, later on.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{дальнейший}} is built on \emph{\ru{дальний}} \textquotedblleft{}distant\textquotedblright{} with the superlative suffix \emph{-\ru{ейш}-}; \emph{\ru{дальний}} comes from \emph{\ru{даль}} \textquotedblleft{}distance\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Proto-Slavic \emph{dalĭ} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
